concepts.def: Durkheim (1893): schools transmit shared norms and create social solidarity; Parsons saw schools as a bridge from family to wider society.
Bowles and Gintis (1976): correspondence principle - schools mirror workplaces, reproducing capitalist hierarchy.
Unwritten lessons (punctuality, obedience, respect for authority) taught alongside the formal curriculum.
Becker (1971) found teachers labelled middle-class students as 'ideal'; can trigger self-fulfilling prophecy.
Lack of money for resources (books, internet, tuition); strong predictor of educational underachievement.
Bourdieu (1977): middle-class knowledge, language and behaviour valued in schools, giving advantage.
